source_text: Τί τὴν κατάραν τοῦ Κάϊν ἐφ' ἑαυ τὸν ἐπισπᾶσαι, τρέμων καὶ περιφερόμενος διὰ παντὸς τοῦ βίου; Οὐ γὰρ ἔχον τὸ σῶμα τὸν ἐκ τῆς φύσεως στηριγμὸν, ἀναγκαίως πεοιδονεῖται καὶ κα τασείεται. Μέχρι πότε οἶνος; μέχρι τίνος μέθη; Κινδυνεύεις λοιπὸν βόρβορος εἶναι ἀντὶ ἀνθρώπου, οὕτως ὅλος ἀνεμίχθης τῷ οἴνῳ, καὶ συγκατεσάπης αὐτῷ, ἐκ τῆς καθημερινῆς κραιπάλης οἴνου ἀπόζων, καὶ τούτου διεφθαρμένου, ὥσπερ τῶν ἀγγείων τὰ ἀχρηστότατα. Τούτους Ἡσαΐας ὀδύρεται· Οὐαὶ οἱ ἐγει ρόμενοι τὸ πρωῒ, καὶ τὸ σίκερα διώκοντες, οἱ μένον τες τὸ ὀψέ· ὁ γὰρ οἶνος αὐτοὺς συγκαύσει· μετὰ γὰρ κιθάρας καὶ αὐλῶν τὸν οἶνον πίνουσι, τὰ δὲ ἔργα Κυρίου οὐκ ἐμβλέπουσι, καὶ τὰ ἔργα τῶν χειρῶν αὐτοῦ οὐ κατανοοῦσι. Σίκερα πᾶν τὸ δυνάμενον μέ θην ἐμποιῆσαι πόμα τοῖς Ἑβραίοις ὀνομάζειν σύνηθες. Οἱ οὖν ἀρχομένης ἡμέρας περισκοποῦντες, ποῦ πότοι γίνονται, καὶ οἰνοπώλια καὶ καπηλεῖα περιαθροῦντες, καὶ ἀλλήλους ἐπὶ τὸ πίνειν παραλαμβάνοντες, καὶ πᾶσαν τῆς ψυχῆς τὴν μέριμναν περὶ τὴν τῶν τοιού των φροντίδα καταναλίσκοντες, οὗτοι ὑπὸ τοῦ προφήτου καταθρηνοῦνται, ὡς καιρὸν οὐδένα ἑαυτοῖς πρὸς τὴν τῶν θαυμασίων τοῦ Θεοῦ κατανόησιν ἀπολείποντες. Οὐ γὰρ ἄγουσι σχολὴν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτῶν ἀνανεῦσαι πρὸς οὐρανὸν, καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτῷ κάλλη καταμαθεῖν, καὶ πᾶσαν τὴν ἐν τοῖς οὖσι διακόσμησιν ἐπισκέψασθαι, ὥστε ἐκ τῆς τούτων εὐταξίας τὸν δημιουργὸν ἐννοῆσαι· ἀλλ' εὐθὺς ἀρχομένης ἡμέρας κοσμοῦσιν ἑαυτῶν τὰ συμπόσια τάπησι ποικίλοις καὶ ἀνθίνοις παραπετάσμασι, σπουδήν τε καὶ ἐπιμέλειαν εἰς τὴν τῶν ἐκπωμάτων παρασκευὴν ἐπιδείκνυνται, ψυκτῆρας καὶ κρατῆρας καὶ φιάλας, ὥσπερ ἐν πομ πῇ τινι καὶ πανηγύρει, διατιθέντες, ὡς ἂν τὸ τῶν ἀγγείων διάφορον τὸν κόρον αὐτοῖς ὑποκλέπτῃ, καὶ ἡ τῶν ἐκπωμάτων ὑπαλλαγὴ καὶ μετάβασις ἱκα νὴν αὐτοῖς εἰς τὸ πίνειν διατριβὴν ἐμποιῇ. Συμποσίαρχοι δέ τινες ἐπὶ τούτοις καὶ ἀρχιοινοχόοι, καὶ ἀρχιτρίκλινοι· καὶ τάξις ἐν ἀταξίᾳ, καὶ διάθεσις ἐν ἀκόσμῳ πράγματι ἐπινενόηται, ἵν', ὥσπερ ταῖς ἀρ χαῖς ταῖς ἔξωθεν ἐκ τῶν δορυφορούντων ἡ σεμνότης συναύξεται, οὕτω καὶ τῇ μέθῃ οἷον βασιλίδι τινὶ θερα πείαν περιστήσαντες, τὸ ἐπονείδιστον αὐτῆς τῷ ὑπερβάλλοντι τῆς σπουδῆς περιστέλλωσι. Στέφανοι ἐπὶ τούτοις καὶ ἄνθη καὶ μύρα καὶ θυμιάματα, καὶ μυρίαι τινὲς ἔξωθεν θυμηδίαι, πλείονα τὴν ἀσχολίαν τοῖς ἀπολλυμένοις παρασκευάζουσιν. Εἶτα πόῤῥω προϊόντος τοῦ πότου, ἅμιλλαι περὶ τοῦ πλείονος, φιλονεικίαι καὶ ἀγωνίσματα, ἀλλήλους ὑπερβάλλεσθαι φιλοτιμουμένων κατὰ τὴν μέθην· καὶ ὁ ἀγωνοθετῶν αὐτοῖς ὁ διάβολος, καὶ ἆθλον τῆς νίκης ἡ ἁμαρτία. Ὁ γὰρ πλείονα τὸν ἄκρατον ἐκχεόμενος, οὗτος φέρεται κατὰ τῶν ἄλλων τὰ νικητήρια. Ὄντως Ἡ δόξα ἐν τῇ αἰσχύνῃ αὐτῶν. Φιλονεικοῦσι μὲν γὰρ ἀλλήλοις, ἀμύνονται δὲ ἑαυτούς. Ποῖος λόγος ἐφικέσθαι τῆς αἰσχρότητος τῶν γινομένων δύναται; Πάντα ἀλογίας γέμει, πάντα συγχύσεως οἱ ἡττηθέντες μεθύουσιν, οἱ νικῶντες μεθύουσιν, οἱ ὑπηρέται καταγελῶσιν. Ἡ χεὶρ ἀπείρηκε, τὸ στόμα οὐχ ὑποδέχεται, ἡ γαστὴρ διαῤῥήγνυται, καὶ τὸ κακὸν οὐχ ὑφίησι. Τὸ ἄθλιον σῶμα, τοῦ φυσικοῦ τόνου παραλυθὲν, ἀπόῤῥυτόν ἐστι πανταχόθεν, τὴν ἐκ τῆς ἀμε τρίας βίαν μὴ ὑπομένον. Ἐλεεινὸν θέαμα Χριστιανῶν ὀφθαλμοῖς ἀνὴρ ἀκμάζων καθ' ἡλικίαν, σφριγῶν τῷ σώματι, στρατιωτικοῖς καταλόγοις ἐμπρέπων, φοράδην οἵκαδε κο μιζόμενος, μὴ δυνάμενος ὀρθοῦσθαι, μηδὲ τοῖς ἰδίοις ποσὶν ἀπιέναι.
thought_title: The voluntary curse of Cain and the pomp of drinking parties
orientation: Basil is rebuking drunkards, having just described the physical ruin drunkenness brings; he now turns to the curse they draw on themselves and the elaborate sham of their drinking parties.
pass_a_gloss: Why do you draw the curse of Cain upon yourself, trembling and being carried about through the whole of life? For the body, not having the support from nature, is necessarily shaken and convulsed. Until when wine? Until when drunkenness? You are in danger henceforth of being mud instead of a human being, so wholly have you been mixed with the wine, and have rotted away with it, stinking of wine from the daily hangover, and of wine that is spoiled, like the most useless of vessels. These Isaiah laments: Woe, those who rise at dawn and pursue strong drink, those who stay till evening; for the wine will burn them; for with harp and pipes they drink wine, but the works of the Lord they do not regard, and the works of his hands they do not consider. Strong drink is the customary name among the Hebrews for every drink able to produce drunkenness. Those, then, who at the beginning of the day look around for where drinking bouts happen, and peer around at wine shops and taverns, and take one another along to drink, and spend all the care of the soul on concern for such things, these are lamented by the prophet, as leaving themselves no time for the contemplation of the wonders of God. For their eyes have no leisure to look up to heaven, and to learn the beauties in it, and to survey all the order in the things that exist, so as from the good order of these to perceive the Creator; but straightaway at the beginning of the day they adorn their drinking parties with varied carpets and flowered curtains, and they display zeal and care for the preparation of the cups, arranging coolers and mixing bowls and saucers, as in some procession and festival, so that the variety of the vessels may steal away their satiety, and the change and transition of the cups may produce for them sufficient pastime for drinking. And certain masters of the drinking party over these, and chief wine-pourers, and chief stewards of the dining room; and order in disorder, and arrangement in a disorderly business has been devised, so that, just as for the magistracies outside, dignity is increased by the bodyguards, so also, having set around drunkenness as around some queen a retinue, they cloak her disgrace by the excess of their zeal. Crowns on top of these, and flowers and perfumes and incenses, and countless outside delights prepare more occupation for those who are perishing. Then, as the drinking goes far forward, contests for the greater amount, rivalries and competitions, of those who are eager to surpass one another in drunkenness; and the one who presides over their contest is the devil, and the prize of victory is sin. For the one who pours out more unmixed wine, this one carries off the victory tokens against the others. Truly their glory is in their shame. For they contend with one another, but they defend themselves against themselves. What word can reach the shamefulness of what happens? Everything is full of unreason, everything of confusion: the defeated are drunk, the victors are drunk, the servants mock. The hand has given out, the mouth does not receive, the belly is bursting, and the evil does not let up. The wretched body, paralyzed from its natural tone, is flowing away on every side, not enduring the violence from excess. A pitiable sight for the eyes of Christians: a man in the prime of age, vigorous in body, distinguished in the military rolls, being carried home on a litter, unable to stand upright, nor to go away on his own feet.

pass_b_english: Why do you draw Cain's curse upon yourself, trembling and wandering through your whole life? For when the body lacks its natural support, it is inevitably shaken and convulsed. How long will wine go on? How long will drunkenness? You are in danger of being mud instead of a man, so completely have you been mixed with wine and rotted away with it, stinking of wine from your daily hangover—and this too spoiled, like the most useless of vessels. Isaiah laments over such people: "Woe to those who rise early in the morning and chase after strong drink, who linger late into the evening, for wine inflames them. They drink wine with lyres and flutes, but they do not regard the works of the Lord, nor consider the work of His hands" (Isaiah 5:11-12). The Hebrews customarily call every drink that can produce drunkenness "strong drink." So those who at daybreak look around for where drinking parties are happening, who peer about at wine shops and taverns, who invite one another to drink, and who spend all the soul's concern on attending to such things—these are the ones the prophet laments, because they leave themselves no time to contemplate the wonders of God. Their eyes have no leisure to look up to heaven and learn its beauties, or to examine the whole order of creation, so that from its arrangement they might perceive the Creator. Instead, as soon as day begins, they adorn their drinking parties with embroidered tapestries and flowered curtains, and they show zeal and care in preparing the cups, arranging coolers and mixing bowls and saucers as if for some procession or festival, so that the variety of vessels may steal away their satiety, and the changing and passing of cups may give them ample occupation in drinking. And on top of this there are presidents of the drinking party, chief wine-pourers, and masters of the banquet: order has been devised in disorder, and arrangement in a chaotic affair, so that just as the dignity of public offices is increased by their attendants, so too they surround drunkenness with a kind of royal service, and by the excess of their zeal they cover over her disgrace. Then come garlands and flowers and perfumes and incense, and countless other external pleasures, which provide still more occupation for those who are perishing. Then, as the drinking goes on and on, there are contests for who can drink more, rivalries and competitions, as they strive to outdo one another in drunkenness. The devil presides over their contest, and the prize of victory is sin. For the one who pours down the most unmixed wine carries off the victory over the others. Truly "their glory is in their shame" (Philippians 3:19). They compete with one another, but it is themselves they punish. What words can reach the shamefulness of what happens? Everything is full of unreason, everything of confusion: the defeated are drunk, the victors are drunk, the servants laugh. The hand grows weary, the mouth cannot receive more, the belly is bursting, and the evil does not let up. The wretched body, its natural tone paralyzed, flows out on every side, unable to endure the violence of excess. A pitiful sight for Christian eyes: a man in the prime of life, vigorous in body, distinguished in the military rolls, carried home on a litter, unable to stand upright or to go on his own feet.

problems.why: Source says 'and this [wine] being spoiled, like the most useless of vessels'—the body is compared to spoiled wine and useless vessels.
problems.fix: stinking of wine from your daily hangover—and this too spoiled, like the most useless of vessels.
